claims.claim: TRG DataCenters' August 2026 ranking of 24 US states gives Virginia a readiness score of 100, followed by Ohio at 88.2, Tennessee at 83.7, Georgia at 81.8 and Texas at 80.8.
claims.episode_span: TRG DataCenters' August 2026 ranking of 24 US states puts Virginia first, with a readiness score of 100.
claims.source_title: Virginia Tops AI Data Center Readiness Ranking as Smaller Markets Advance
claims.supporting_quote: Virginia received a readiness score of 100, followed by Ohio at 88.2, Tennessee at 83.7, Georgia at 81.8, and Texas at 80.8.

claims.claim: TRG's dataset maps seven large AI sites in Virginia totaling 1,085 MW, 1,410 MW in Ohio and 1,373 MW in Tennessee, and those figures are not each state's total data-centre market.
claims.episode_span: TRG's dataset maps seven large AI sites in Virginia totaling 1,085 MW, against 1,410 MW in Ohio and 1,373 MW in Tennessee
claims.source_title: Virginia Tops AI Data Center Readiness Ranking as Smaller Markets Advance
claims.supporting_quote: TRG’s dataset mapped seven large AI sites in Virginia totaling 1,085 MW of capacity, while Ohio and Tennessee showed higher mapped capacities – 1,410 MW in Ohio and 1,373 MW in Tennessee.

claims.claim: Chris Hinkle said Ohio's mapped AI capacity was around 30 percent greater and that the grid serving Virginia's facilities had roughly one-third lower carbon intensity, with about 2.3 million tons of CO2 a year for Virginia's dataset facilities versus roughly 4.5 million in Ohio and 4.3 million in Tennessee.
claims.episode_span: He tied the dataset's AI facilities to around 2.3 million tons of CO2 a year in Virginia, compared with roughly 4.5 million tons in Ohio and 4.3 million tons in Tennessee.
claims.source_title: Virginia Tops AI Data Center Readiness Ranking as Smaller Markets Advance
claims.supporting_quote: “As a result, the AI facilities in our dataset are associated with around 2.3 million tons of CO2 emissions annually, compared with roughly 4.5 million tons in Ohio and 4.3 million in Tennessee,” he said.

claims.claim: Xsight Labs raised over $300 million led by Fidelity Management & Research Company for programmable DPUs and Ethernet switches, including a DPU with 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores at full 800 Gbps and a 12.8 Tbps switch under 200 watts at sub-700-nanosecond latency.
claims.episode_span: The 12.8 Tbps Ethernet switch is specified at deterministic, sub-700-nanosecond latency and under 200 watts.
claims.supporting_quote: The company’s 12.8 Tbps Ethernet switch operates at deterministic, sub-700ns latency under 200W.

claims.supporting_quote: Tesla and SpaceX will aim to make and test about 10 chip designs a year at Terafab's Giga Texas research fab, CEO Elon Musk said, accelerating a development process he says can take two years for one significant design to hit volume production.
